link:https://doi.org/10.1186/s40854-026-.reader_what: The paper investigates the role of financial technologies (FinTech) in advancing green public procurement (GPP) across 33 European countries—including the
link:https://doi.org/10.1186/s40854-026-.reader_more: The paper investigates the role of financial technologies (FinTech) in advancing green public procurement (GPP) across 33 European countries—including the 27 EU member states—over 2011, 2014, 2017, and 2021. Utilizing logistic regression, linear probability models, OLS, and negative binomial regressions, the analysis assesses how FinTech adoption influences both the likelihood of applying green criteria in public tenders and key GPP outcomes such as competition and pricing. Drawing on contract-level data from the European Union’s Tenders Electronic Daily (TED) database, which provides comprehensive information on public procurement across EU countries, the findings demonstrate a strong positive relationship between FinTech adoption and GPP performance: countries with higher FinTech penetration show significantly greater use of green criteria, more competitive bidding, and lower procurement costs.

link:https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21048.reader_more: Recent price shocks have prompted calls to curb Europe's dependence on fossil gas imports, but the cost of this goal, and the consumer protection it affords, remain uncertain. link:https://doi.org/10.1177/2336825x261.reader_title: Ukraine and the transformation of French strategic imaginaries: The discursive reconfiguration of European strategic autonomy under the presidency
link:https://doi.org/10.1177/2336825x261.reader_what: Ukraine and the transformation of French strategic imaginaries: The discursive reconfiguration of European strategic autonomy under the presidency of Emmanuel
link:https://doi.org/10.1177/2336825x261.reader_more: Ukraine and the transformation of French strategic imaginaries: The discursive reconfiguration of European strategic autonomy under the presidency of Emmanuel Macron (2017-2026). historical:id:75f06d790703e337.reader_what: The infographic explains EU sanctions procedures and trade, finance and technology restrictions, with Russia as the case.
historical:id:75f06d790703e337.reader_why: Sanctions restrict access to assets, transactions and strategic imports, but economic costs need not produce political compliance.
historical:id:75f06d790703e337.reader_more: Sylvie Matelly distinguishes targeted sanctions from broad restrictions and explains how EU restrictive measures are decided. The Russia case illustrates asset freezes, banking restrictions, dual-use technology controls and energy trade limits. The infographic also notes opportunities for evasion and adaptation. It is historical policy education, not a causal estimate of sanctions effectiveness or a record of 2026 sanctions totals.
